summary: Tioconazole is an imidazole (azole) antifungal used topically and intravaginally to treat vulvovaginal candidiasis. The over-the-counter product is a 6.5% vaginal ointment delivering 300 mg of tioconazole in a single 4.6 g prefilled applicator inserted at bedtime. It inhibits fungal ergosterol synthesis, damaging the fungal cell membrane and killing the overgrowth of Candida. Systemic absorption is minimal, and treatment is a single dose.
indications: Treatment of vulvovaginal candidiasis (vaginal yeast infection) in adults and adolescents 12 years and older
Topical 1% formulations: treatment of susceptible dermatophyte and yeast skin infections

dosage.d: Insert the entire contents of one applicator (4.6 g of 6.5% ointment, providing 300 mg tioconazole) into the vagina
dosage.n: For adults and children 12 years and older; children under 12 should consult a doctor

dosage.d: Apply 1% tioconazole cream to the affected area as directed
dosage.n: Duration depends on the specific infection treated

admin: For vaginal use only; insert the entire applicator contents at bedtime
Use the single prefilled applicator as supplied; one dose completes therapy
Do not use tampons, douches, or spermicides during treatment
Note that the petrolatum base may damage condoms and diaphragms, which can then fail to prevent pregnancy or sexually transmitted infection
A small amount of ointment may leak from the vagina; a sanitary pad may be used
moa: Tioconazole is an imidazole antifungal that inhibits the fungal cytochrome P450 enzyme lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase, blocking the conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol. Depletion of ergosterol and accumulation of toxic sterol precursors disrupt the integrity and function of the fungal cell membrane, leading to growth inhibition and death of Candida and other susceptible fungi.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to tioconazole or other imidazole antifungals
Self-treatment in a person who has never had a vaginal yeast infection diagnosed by a doctor
relative: First episode of vaginal symptoms (should be evaluated by a clinician)
Frequently recurring yeast infections (evaluate for underlying cause such as diabetes or immunocompromise)
Fever, chills, lower abdominal/back/shoulder pain, or foul-smelling discharge (suggests other infection)
monitor: Local irritation that worsens or does not improve

preg: If pregnant or breastfeeding, ask a health professional before use. Systemic absorption after intravaginal application is minimal; nonetheless self-treatment in pregnancy should be guided by a clinician.
lact: If pregnant or breastfeeding, ask a health professional before use. Systemic absorption is minimal with intravaginal use, so exposure of a breastfed infant is expected to be low.
renal: No dosage adjustment is needed; systemic absorption after intravaginal or topical use is negligible.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is needed; systemic absorption after intravaginal or topical use is negligible.

major: No clinically significant systemic drug interactions expected with intravaginal use
moderate: The petrolatum-based ointment can weaken latex condoms and diaphragms, reducing contraceptive and barrier protection
minor: Concurrent intravaginal products (spermicides, douches) may interfere with therapy
interactions.diagnostics: No significant effect on common laboratory tests

common: Mild increase in vaginal burning, itching, or irritation
emergency: Severe allergic reaction (rash, swelling, difficulty breathing) - stop use and seek emergency care

monitoring: Improvement of vaginal symptoms, expected within a few days
Reassessment by a clinician if no improvement in 3 days or symptoms persist beyond 7 days
Evaluation for other causes if symptoms recur within 2 months or with systemic symptoms

pk: Local antifungal action begins after insertion; symptom relief typically within a few days
Acts locally in the vagina; systemic plasma levels are very low

pearls: Single 4.6 g dose of 6.5% ointment delivers 300 mg tioconazole - convenient one-time therapy
Petrolatum base can degrade latex condoms and diaphragms for up to 3 days
First-ever vaginal symptoms should be evaluated by a clinician rather than self-treated
Minimal systemic absorption makes systemic interactions and organ-based dose adjustments unnecessary
Lack of improvement may indicate a non-Candida cause or resistant organism
missed: This is a single-dose treatment, so there is no scheduled repeat dose. If the applicator contents were not fully inserted, complete the single application at bedtime. Do not use more than one applicator unless directed by a clinician.
overdose: Overdose is unlikely with intravaginal use given minimal systemic absorption. Accidental ingestion of the ointment may cause gastrointestinal upset; treat supportively. Contact Poison Control (1-800-222-1222) for guidance.
